external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches to the self-hosted git server and may log in to the build runner to start a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: git server
processes.description: The self-hosted git server receiving developer branches and providing source for builds.
processes.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: The runner that fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to start rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: The controller that receives release requests and provides the current release to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small back-office server at each store that checks the current release, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office running the till software as a container.
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores; this element represents the store-server component across the estate.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry storing finished container images tagged with commit SHA values and serving them to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: current release record
data_stores.description: The record held by the deploy controller identifying which image SHA the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and kicks off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server after a merge starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.notes: A merge to main starts a build.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: Authentication uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: read release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it. The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment where the build runner and image registry run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The in-store estate containing the store servers in store back offices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the store estate over the WAN
